questions.prompt: best 20000mAh power bank for MacBook Air
questions.why: Apple fast-charges the MacBook Air with its 70 W adapter (support.apple.com/102378), so a 65 W port cannot fast-charge it and the next USB-C step a power bank offers is a 100 W port; 20,000 mAh (about 72-74 Wh) is the size that gives about one full Air charge (Macworld measured a 72 Wh bank filling a 13-inch Air with about 5% to spare). The page keeps to 20,000 mAh class banks with at least one 100 W or higher USB-C port.
questions.notes: Ours: UGREEN Nexode 20K 130W ($54.99, no record yet), Baseus FC41 20K 100W with two built-in cables ($59.99 white, no record yet), UGREEN Nexode 20K 100W bundle (record). Rivals: Cuktech 15 Ultra (~$67 Amazon per Macworld; check whether it is 20K or 25K), Anker Prime 20K ($119.99), Anker 20K 87W (USB-C caps at 65 W: left out). Search suggestions include 'best power bank for macbook air m5 / m4'.

questions.prompt: best 10000mAh power bank with built-in cable
questions.why: 10,000 mAh is the daily-carry size shoppers search most, and 'power bank with built in cable 10000mah' is a standing search suggestion; 45 W from the cable covers the iPhone 17 Pro Max's roughly 36 W peak (ChargerLAB via 9to5Mac) and Samsung's 45 W Super Fast Charging 2.0 when the bank supports PPS at 10 V / 4.5 A. The page keeps to 10,000 mAh banks with a cable built in.
questions.notes: Ours: UGREEN Nexode Pro 10K 45W built-in cable ($35.99, no record yet), Baseus FC11 10K dual cables 45W ($35.99, no record yet), Baseus FC41 10K 67W dual cables ($69.99, no record yet), Anker Nano 10K 45W (record, Amazon link). Rivals: INIU 45W (~$29.99 list). PPS support on the UGREEN and Baseus 10K is unverified: check the makers' pages.

questions.why: 25,000 mAh (about 90 Wh) is the largest common size under the FAA's 100 Wh carry-on limit without airline approval (faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe), and $100 is the price tier shoppers search for this size. The page keeps to 25,000-27,600 mAh banks under 100 Wh priced at or under $100 on the date read.
questions.notes: Ours: UGREEN 145W 25K ($59.98; reviews disagree whether its 140 W port is PD 3.1 and whether it supports PPS: check UGREEN's current spec), Baseus FC41 25K 145W (code price in our table), UGREEN Nexode 200W 25K (code price in our table), AOHi Black Warrior 25.2K (store now $89.99 per the 11-26 desk read), AOHi Future Starship 27.6K. Rivals: Sharge HyperTower 170 ($79.90; Macworld's best tested score in this group), Cuktech 15 Ultra / 25 SE, EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27K ($89 Amazon 11-18), Anker Laptop 25K ($91), INIU P64 ($88.99).

questions.why: 40,000-48,000 mAh banks are 144-154 Wh: above the FAA's 100 Wh line, so they need airline approval (two at most, carry-on only) and some airlines refuse them; that makes this size a desk, camping or road-trip choice for one and a half to two laptop charges. The page keeps to banks of 40,000 mAh or more with a USB-C port of at least 100 W, and says the airline rule plainly.
questions.notes: Ours: UGREEN 48000mAh 300W ($118.99, no record yet; Macworld's high-capacity pick, about 1.8 charges of a 14-inch MacBook Pro), AOHi Starship 40K 146 Wh (record). Rivals: Cuktech 30 ($150-180), Anker Prime 26K is not this size. Weights: AOHi 40K 916 g vs UGREEN 48K 1,637 g (check both).

questions.prompt: best portable monitor for MacBook Pro 16
questions.why: The 16-inch MacBook Pro's own screen is 16:10 at up to 120 Hz, so the panel that matches it is a 16-inch 16:10 screen at 2560x1600 and 120 Hz (text at 1080p looks soft with macOS scaling at this size); 'best portable monitor for macbook pro 16' is a standing search suggestion. The page ranks 16-inch screens on that match first, then brightness and weight.
questions.notes: Store reads 2026-11-26 evening in the Agent Chrome (product page text and Shopify .js; re-read anything you cite): UPERFECT GR16EQ (formerly UGame C2 Pro), https://uperfect.com/products/2k-144hz-gaming-monitor: 16-inch 2560x1600 144 Hz, 450 cd/m2, 188.68 ppi, FreeSync, 2 full-featured USB-C + mini HDMI, driver free, weight stated twice (0.75 kg / 1.66 lb in the copy, net 1.04 kg / 2.3 lb in the spec table: say so), $199.99 (compare-at $329.99), available. SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2, https://www.sotsu.com/products/flipaction-pro-16: 2560x1600 120 Hz, 400 nits, 11 W max, monitor 930 g + base stand 435 g, $599.50 list, $509.58 with 15% off shown, in stock (SOTSU Elite 16 is 4K 60 Hz, pre-order to Dec 11: not in the line). Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro (ours), https://www.mobilepixels.us/products/duex-float: $247.99 (regular $389.99), 2560x1600, 2.9 lb, two USB-C with 65 W pass-through, the only one that stacks above the laptop screen. Skip only if neither a store-linked product nor an Amazon-reachable rival is in the top three. questions.prompt: best laptop screen extender for 13-inch laptop
questions.why: 13-13.6 inches (the MacBook Air 13 and most ultrabooks) is the smallest common laptop size and many extenders' fit ranges start above it; 'laptop screen extender 13 inch' and 'for macbook air 13 inch' are search suggestions. Base M1-M3 MacBook Airs drive one external screen with the lid open. The page keeps to extenders whose maker's fit range includes 13-inch laptops.
questions.notes: Leads (all three ours): Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS (13.3-inch, 1.3 lb, no driver; 300 nits is the maker's figure, a 2022 review measured the older model at 152 nits), FOPO S7 (fits from 12-inch per FOPO; both screens light only on an M4 Air), Trio 3 Pro (Macworld lists 13-16-inch MacBooks; second screen needs Mobile Pixels' driver on M1-M3). Rivals: SideTrak Swivel 13.3 / 14 ($319.99+), Xebec Tri-Screen 2 ($299, 10.1-inch screens).

questions.prompt: best laptop screen extender for MacBook Air 15
questions.why: The 15.3-inch MacBook Air sits inside the 15-16-inch fit range most extenders are sized for, and 'laptop screen extender for macbook air 15' is a search suggestion; the line that decides it is how many external screens the Air drives (M2 and M3 one with the lid open, M4 two), so the page ranks by what works on each chip first.
questions.notes: Leads: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS (ours, one cable, works on any Air), Duex Float 2 Pro (ours, stacked above), Trio 3 Pro (ours; driver for the second screen on M2/M3), FOPO S10/S11 (ours; check fit and video path), Kefeya S6 ($227; driver need unverified). questions.prompt: lightest laptop screen extender under 2 lb
questions.why: Under 2 lb is the backpack line for screens that travel with a laptop: Wirecutter found the lightest portable screens at about 1.5 lb and most at 1.7 to over 3 lb, and screens that clip to the lid put that weight on the laptop's hinge. 'lightest laptop screen extender' is a search suggestion. The page keeps to extenders whose maker-stated weight is under 2 lb (say whose figure, and whether it includes the mount).
questions.notes: Leads: Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS (ours, 1.3 lb), Duex Max DS (ours, 1.8 lb), SideTrak Swivel (~1.5 lb per B&H for an older model, $319.99+), Xebec Tri-Screen 2 (exactly 2 lb: just over the line, name it as left out). Weights from retailer listings must be checked on the maker's page.

The page keeps to TMR-sensor boards at or under $100 on the date read, and says plainly that TMR is not a proven upgrade over Hall effect once calibrated (Wooting, TechRadar).
